criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs builds a base commit and a candidate commit whose athena.toml contains an unknown field. admit() must return a violation with rule "configuration", the path athena.toml, and a detail that names the parse error and says how to repair it. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.
criteria.evidence: The test an_unknown_field_in_athena_toml_is_a_configuration_violation builds a base commit, then a candidate that adds a [bogus] table. It checks for exactly one configuration violation with path athena.toml and a detail containing "does not parse", "bogus" and "Repair it". It passed. It calls admit_without_secrets, the helper that admit() wraps and only adds the secret scan to, so admit() returns the same configuration violation.

criteria.criterion: A second test covers an unknown field in defaults.toml: admit() returns a configuration violation for the path defaults.toml. A third test shows that a candidate whose athena.toml and defaults.toml both parse, and a candidate that touches neither file, add no configuration violation. Run `cargo test -p athena-core admission`.
criteria.evidence: Both tests passed: an_unknown_field_in_defaults_toml_is_a_configuration_violation, and parsing_configuration_and_untouched_configuration_add_no_violation, which covers both files edited but still parsing and a candidate that changes only a.txt.

criteria.criterion: admit() parses the candidate's athena.toml and defaults.toml only when they changed, using Config::parse and DefaultsModel::parse from athena-data (the same parsers the gate uses). It does not duplicate the schema. A deleted file is not parsed. The violation reaches the existing candidate.violations path in run.rs, so the job is rejected with the finding before landing.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The new loop runs only over input.changes, skips ChangeStatus::Deleted and any path other than CONFIG_PATH or DEFAULTS_PATH, reads the candidate's copy with show_file, and calls Config::parse or DefaultsModel::parse, matching content.rs lines 84-90. In run.rs, the admission violations become candidate.violations at line 682, followed by self.failure and an early return before the verifier snapshot and landing.

criteria.criterion: The module doc comment in admission.rs lists the new rule. A parse failure is reported as an admission violation (the finding), not as an anyhow error that aborts the job.
criteria.evidence: The module doc gains a bullet: a changed `athena.toml` or `defaults.toml` does not parse (rule `configuration`). The parse error is turned into a string with .err().map(...) and pushed as a violation. Only git failures still propagate as errors through `?`.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, including the existing athena-gate content tests for the configuration rule.
criteria.evidence: Athena reported that fmt, clippy with -D warnings, and cargo test --locked (590 tests) all passed on this tree. I ran cargo test -p athena-gate content: 13 passed, including content::tests::a_configuration_that_does_not_parse_is_refused.

findings.summary: The tests call admit_without_secrets, not admit(), so they skip the gitleaks secret scan.
findings.evidence: admit_files calls admit_without_secrets(&AdmissionInput{..}). admit() only appends secret findings to that result, so the configuration behavior is the same. The test comment says gitleaks is not needed.

findings.summary: No test covers a deleted athena.toml or defaults.toml, so nothing checks the deleted-file skip.
findings.evidence: admit_files always records ChangeStatus::Modified. The Deleted branch is covered only by reading the code.

summary: The change does what the request asks. Candidate admission in admission.rs now parses a changed athena.toml or defaults.toml with the same parsers the gate uses at landing (Config::parse and DefaultsModel::parse). It skips deleted files. A parse failure becomes a "configuration" PolicyViolation whose detail names the parse error and says how to repair it. run.rs already puts admission violations into candidate.violations and rejects the job before landing, so run.rs did not need editing. Three new tests cover an unknown field in athena.toml, an unknown field in defaults.toml, and two clean cases: both files edited but still parsing, and neither file touched. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core admission` and `cargo test -p athena-gate content` in this snapshot and both passed. Athena's own fmt, clippy and full test runs had already passed. The only changed files are admission.rs and CHANGELOG.md, both on the deliverables list. Minor gaps: the tests call admit_without_secrets, a new helper that admit() wraps, so they skip the gitleaks secret scan; and no test covers a deleted config file.
